# Personaudit

> Point it at a public URL in the hosted app, or at a URL behind a login via the CLI.
> Hosted scans never see a password. CLI scans keep the saved session on your machine
> and run axe-core at every state reached.

## What it does

Personaudit has two modes, and the split reflects what the evidence actually supports:

- **Scan (the core).** Crawls the site with a saved session — behind the login wall — and
  runs **axe-core** at every state reached, reporting deterministic, citable WCAG rule
  violations. This is the part nothing free replaces: the `axe` CLI does not crawl and
  does not hold a session. Gate-able in CI on newly-introduced defects. The hosted grader
  is the public-pages-only version of this scan.
- **Run (UX personas).** Adds LLM personas (a first-time visitor, a mobile user on slow
  3G) that browse toward a goal. Their unique output is **task success** — did a
  real-shaped user actually complete the flow? — which a crawler cannot produce. Their
  finding output is *opinion* (jargon, buried pricing, tap targets): useful, never a
  compliance verdict.

## What it is NOT

- **Not a disability simulator.** There is no "blind user" or other disabled-user persona,
  and there will not be one — an LLM roleplaying a disability is inaccurate and harmful.
  Personas are ordinary-user UX opinion only.
- **Personas do not judge accessibility compliance.** Only axe-core touches compliance;
  it is deterministic and citable. A head-to-head test found personas do not surface
  accessibility defects a scripted crawler misses, so they are not pitched as an
  accessibility tool — their validated, distinct value is task success.

## Who it's for

Agencies and freelancers who carry accessibility liability across many client sites and
need defensible, repeatable evidence across authenticated states — in CI and as a
client-facing report.

## Tech

- axe-core for accessibility scanning (the compliance verdict)
- Playwright for real-browser crawling behind a saved session
- Anthropic Claude for the UX personas (navigation + task-success judgment)
- CLI (`mpersonas`) and web app
